evidence.description: The notification observer is added to the notificationCenter but is stored in a dictionary that is accessed and modified across different threads (via observerQueue).
The page load observer is added and stored in the authTabObservers dictionary without using the observerQueue barrier, potentially leading to a race condition with other writes to the dictionary.

candidates.explanation: The code lacks consistent synchronization when adding observers to the `authTabObservers` dictionary. While `setupAutoCloseForTab` uses a barrier, `setupPageLoadMonitoring` (called by `createObserver`) writes to the dictionary directly without using the `observerQueue` barrier, creating a thread-safety risk.
candidates.title: Thread-Safety Violation on Dictionary Access

evidence.description: A nested async call is made to handle authentication completion after a delay.
The handleAuthenticationCompletion method uses a barrier on the observerQueue.

candidates.explanation: The logic for handling page load completion uses a delayed `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter` call which then triggers `handleAuthenticationCompletion`. This pattern can lead to race conditions where a fallback timeout might trigger and attempt to clean up the same tab simultaneously with the delayed page load completion, as there is no state check to see if the tab is already being processed.
candidates.title: Potential Race Condition in Completion Handling

evidence.description: The trackedTabCount property filters keys to count tabs.
The trackedTabUUIDs property filters keys to return tab UUIDs.

candidates.explanation: The logic for identifying unique tabs relies on string parsing (`!$0.contains("_pageload")`). If a tab UUID were to naturally contain the string "_pageload", the count and the list of tracked UUIDs would be incorrect.
candidates.title: Fragile Key Identification Logic
